newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank two-month profits up 21.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank two-month profits up 21.6 pct.

text.p: Germany's Commerzbank AG, which on Monday announced higher 1996 profits, said on Tuesday that developments in the first two months of 1997 pointed to a further increase in profits in the current business year.

Commerzbank chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen said in the text of a speech prepared for delivery to a news conference, "We are completely satisfied with our profit and loss account for January and February 1997. Interest and commission income both rose by around 15th from the previous year."
He said that group operating profit before provisions for bad debt rose 21.6 percent to 626 million marks in the first two months of the year.

Kohlhaussen added "It is still too early to relax on loan loss provisions for lending business. I am confident on the basis of the good strat in this new year that the Commerzbank group can raise its operating result again in 1997."
On Monday, Commerzbank said its group operating profit after provision for bad debt jumped to 1.859 billion marks in 1996 from 1.446 billion in 1995.
